decisions.rationale: Intended Mega is Charizard Y. Garchomp/Raichu immediately punish the Houndoom-Manectric mode: Raichu can deny Houndoom’s setup while Garchomp targets Manectric, avoiding Venusaur’s bad exposure. Into rain, retain single-target options around Wide Guard. Mega Y resets rain later; Primarina closes against the Fire-, Fighting-, and Dragon-facing endgame.
decisions.notebook: Opponent showed Houndoom as Timid Charcoal Flash Fire with Nasty Plot, Dark Pulse, Fire Blast, Protect; it threatens Venusaur and discourages Fire targeting. Manectric is Timid Choice Scarf Lightning Rod with Thunderbolt, Volt Switch, Overheat, Snarl; its Scarf speed and Lightning Rod make Raichu/Charizard positioning important. Pelipper repeatedly used Wide Guard, so single-target pressure is reliable into its rain mode. Sneasler is Adamant White Herb Unburden with Close Combat, Acrobatics, Dire Claw, Protect; Raichu outspeeds it before paralysis and Nuzzle is effective control. Future plan: avoid exposing Venusaur early to Houndoom/Manectric; use Garchomp and Raichu as the main anti-Manectric, Pelipper, and Sneasler core.

decisions.rationale: Lead Pelipper+Sneasler to set rain and safely trigger Sneasler's Unburden (Close Combat → White Herb → 344 Spe, outspeeds everything including Chlorophyll Venusaur). Pelipper's Wide Guard blocks Heat Wave/Rock Slide. Snorlax back provides Thick Fat to resist Charizard-Y Heat Wave and Curse body to tank physical hits. decisions.notebook: Sun mode durable notes (game 1 confirmed): Charizard-Y Drought + Venusaur Chlorophyll FocusSash Modest is the core; Raichu LumBerry LightningRod runs FakeOut + Nuzzle; Garchomp LifeOrb Jolly. Wide Guard ONLY blocks spread moves. Manectric is OHKO'd by Modest Venusaur Earth Power in sun. Houndoom without Mega is too frail. Speed tiers: Sneasler 172 base, 344 after Unburden > Garchomp 134-169 > Charizard-Y 132-167 > Venusaur 100-132 (200-264 in sun) > Pelipper 101. Sneasler Unburden after Close Combat+White Herb = 344 Spe. Sinistcha Grass type immune to powder moves (Sleep Powder redirected via Rage Powder fails). Game 2 plan: Pelipper+Sneasler lead, Snorlax+Sinistcha back. Game 3 contingency: hold Sinistcha Trick Room if opponent pivots to non-sun mode.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out denies Pelipper’s attack, Protect, and Wide Guard this turn while Life Orb Stomping Tantrum guarantees the Sneasler OHKO if it does not Protect. If Sneasler Protects, both foes are denied meaningful progress and Garchomp avoids the rain-boosted Hydro Pump this turn.

Focus fire Garchomp. CC 42.8-76% + Hydro Pump rain 51.2-93.4% = 94-169% combined, likely OHKO. Even if Sneasler flinches from Fake Out, Hydro Pump alone does 51-93%. If Garchomp switches to Charizard-Y, attacks hit the slot (CC big, Hydro Pump moderate in sun). Rock Slide on Pelipper 25-58% is survivable; on Sneasler only 7-18% (NVE). Thunderbolt OHKO is the real threat but Raichu likely commits to Fake Out to stop CC.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper is flinched and locked. Sneasler fainted to Garchomp's SE Stomping Tantrum. Garchomp cannot survive rain-boosted Hydro Pump, so Protect preserves it. Targeting Sinistcha directly avoids Rage Powder disruption, gives paralysis odds to stop Trick Room, and makes its future Trick Room turns less reliable. Thunderbolt Pelipper is freely redirected and Rock Slide loses to Wide Guard.

Raichu T-bolt 4x SE OHKOs Pelipper, so Pelipper must Protect. Sinistcha Shadow Ball is Ghost 2x SE on Dragon/Ground Garchomp at 23% — clean OHKO removing opponent's Life Orb pressure. Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum is 0.5x on Sinistcha; only Rock Slide spread hurts, and Sinistcha's 158/145 bulk with Hospitality Leftovers... wait, Hospitality doesn't heal itself, only ally — but 30-50% from Rock Slide is still survivable. Net: keep Pelipper, remove Garchomp, force opponent to reveal plan.

decisions.rationale: Thunderbolt gives immediate single-target pressure through Wide Guard and removes Pelipper if it does not Protect. Preserve low-HP Garchomp for Manectric while bringing Primarina into a likely Trick Room, where its low Speed is valuable. Raichu moves before Sinistcha, but cannot prevent Trick Room with its listed moves.

Double-targeting Garchomp at 23% guarantees KO (Hydro Pump 31-69% confirmed KO, Shadow Ball 20-44% possible KO). Sinistcha more important than Pelipper long game (only SE answer Charizard-Y via Matcha Gotcha, TR setter). Losing Pelipper to Tbolt acceptable; rain continues 5 more turns. Protect line risks Sinistcha faint to Garchomp Dragon Claw if Shadow Ball misses 50% par. Garchomp likely attacks (higher EV than 33% Protect) so Hydro Pump line protects Sinistcha better.

Curse gives Snorlax +1 Atk/+1 Def, turning it into a TR monster with Leftovers/Thick Fat sustain. Sinistcha survives Primarina Ice Beam (~45%, 97→52). Next turn under TR, +1 Body Slam (~50%) + Matcha Gotcha (~45%) KOs Primarina from 72%. TR also covers endgame vs Charizard-Y/Venusaur sun switch-ins.

Sinistcha acts before Primarina under Trick Room and can redirect, but both attacks still converge on it; Ice Beam supplies the decisive super-effective damage while Thunderbolt adds insurance. Leaving it alive risks Matcha Gotcha pressure and repeated redirection for Snorlax.

decisions.rationale: Aggressive play to pressure Primarina, the biggest threat to Sinistcha. Snorlax Body Slam + Sinistcha Matcha Gotcha (SE 2x on Primarina, spread) puts Primarina in KO range or forces a switch, keeping Sinistcha alive. Sinistcha at 28% cannot survive Primarina's Ice Beam, so must remove the threat.

Primarina cannot safely remain. Charizard is the durable switch and intended Mega, while Raichu Protect denies a possible Body Slam into it during Trick Room. This preserves Garchomp’s Life Orb Ground pressure for Snorlax and avoids spending a move on already-paralyzed Snorlax.

Sinistcha fainted; Snorlax is my last Pokémon. Primarina is at 3% HP — Body Slam into Primarina is a guaranteed KO that removes a threat and forces the opponent to commit a switch or Protect. Trick Room (3 turns) keeps Snorlax moving first despite paralysis. Curse wastes a turn with no damage and only 1 mon remaining; Body Slam Raichu likely fails to KO and leaves Primarina alive to spread damage.

decisions.rationale: Sacrifice the 4% Primarina rather than risk reduced-success Protect on Charizard. Raichu gets guaranteed chip while Trick Room expires; then bring Charizard back, Mega Evolve to establish sun, and pressure Snorlax first with Solar Beam plus Thunderbolt. Preserve Garchomp as a cleaner.

Sacrifice Garchomp rather than expose Charizard to the Body Slam damage range already shown. Preserving Charizard gives the remaining endgame attacker a safer entry and access to Mega Y's Drought-supported Solar Beam pressure next turn.

decisions.rationale: Snorlax moves first in TR (par 25→9975). Body Slam 85BP STAB Adamant 178 Atk vs Charizard 78 Def is near-OHKO from 39% HP per notebook. KOing Charizard removes Mega Evolution and Drought sun setter before opponent can pivot. Even if not full KO, massive damage pressures faint. Sinistcha fainted, Pass only option.

Double-target Snorlax now: Raichu is guaranteed faster and Thunderbolt has already shown meaningful damage, while Garchomp adds immediate Life Orb STAB damage before it is likely removed by Body Slam. This gives the best chance to deny Rest and end the game immediately; Stomping Tantrum is accurate unlike Rock Slide.

Body Slam Garchomp removes the most dangerous threat at 23% HP. Snorlax is paralyzed (25% full para) and slowest, so it moves last. Curse is too risky—Snorlax might get fully paralyzed and eat two hits with no boost. KOing Garchomp cuts opponent to Raichu + Charizard bench, giving Snorlax a winnable 1v2 with Thick Fat neutering Fire and Leftovers recovery.

reflections.summary: Won by bringing the right anti-rain/control four and using Raichu paralysis plus focused single-target pressure to remove Sinistcha, preventing Trick Room/Snorlax from taking over. Charizardite Y was a suitable matchup choice, though Snorlax still made the endgame costly.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the same anti-rain core, but prioritize removing Sinistcha even more decisively before Trick Room goes up; preserve Primarina or Garchomp as a healthier Snorlax answer rather than trading both late.

Sinistcha is Calm Kasib Berry Hospitality with Trick Room, Matcha Gotcha, Shadow Ball, and Rage Powder; it can establish Trick Room despite paralysis, so remove it promptly. Snorlax is Adamant Thick Fat Leftovers with Curse, Body Slam, Rest, and Sleep Talk; deny prolonged setup and retain a healthy dedicated answer.

reflections.summary: Team preview was fundamentally wrong: bringing Pelipper (Drizzle) against a Charizard-Y Mega team meant rain was immediately overridden by Drought, so Pelipper contributed nothing and fainted without value. Sinistcha was too fragile to set Trick Room—Primarina's super-effective Ice Beam plus Raichu's Thunderbolt deleted it on turn 5 before Snorlax could capitalize. Snorlax then absorbed paralysis from Raichu Nuzzle and was chipped down by Life Orb Garchomp + Raichu Thunderbolt, trading one-for-o
reflections.adjustment: Drop Pelipper entirely for game 3. Charizard-Y Drought hard-counters Drizzle, so the rain core is dead on arrival. Replace it with a Pokémon that either ignores sun (e.g., a Chlorophyll sweeper to outrace Charizard-Y, or a Rock/Steel-type that resists Heat Wave) or directly threatens the sun core. Keep Snorlax + Sinistcha as the Trick Room win condition but protect Sinistcha from Primarina—lead Sinistcha with a Fake Out user or position it so Primarina cannot double-target it on the turn Trick R

NEW: Primarina Liquid Voice Sparkling Aria + Moonblast + Ice Beam threatens Sinistcha hard (Ice Beam SE, Moonblast neutral); Primarina survives Snorlax Body Slam from full (~52% with Sitrus proc, not OHKO). NEW: Raichu Nuzzle on turn 4 paralyzed Snorlax immediately—must prevent Raichu from getting a free Nuzzle on the TR setter or win condition. NEW: Garchomp Life Orb Stomping Tantrum + Raichu Thunderbolt cleanly KOs full-HP Snorlax in one turn (observed 100→8% with par chip). NEW: Sinistcha cannot survive Primarina+Raichu double on the Trick Room turn—needs positional support or a different setter (e.g., Sneasler with own speed control, or a bulkier TR user). Game 3 plan: DROP PELIPPER. Lead Sneasler + Snorlax to pressure Charizard-Y physically and set up Curse Body Slam under Trick Room; bring a sun-neutral 4th (Chlorophyll sweeper or Rock/Steel resist). Do not let Raichu Nuzzle Snorlax for free—target Raichu first or position Snorlax behind a Fake Out user.
